generic: It goes better than the plan allowed for, and nobody says so out loud.
Textbook, and then some. The crew is out before the window opened.
Whatever was supposed to be hard about this was not.
Clean enough that it will be told wrong for years.
The job gives up more than it was asked for.
stealth: Not one camera, not one floorboard, not one witness.
The route is walked twice and remembered as empty both times.
They pass a guard close enough to smell his coffee.
The building never notices it had company.
athletics: The line is set, the drop is silent, and the way out is already rigged.
Four storeys in under a minute, and the parapet holds.
The gap gets crossed like it was a step.
They land soft, on the balls of the feet, and keep moving.
combat: Two down, neither hurt badly, and neither able to describe anyone.
It ends before it is a fight, which is the only way it should end.
One sap, one shoulder, one very quiet corridor.
Nobody files a report on being surprised by nothing.
lockpicking: The last pin sets before the tension wrench has finished turning.
The door opens like it was expecting them.
The case comes open, the plate never knows, and the swap is perfect.
Whoever fitted this lock would want to watch that.
hacking: The log rewrites itself into a scheduled maintenance window.
Every camera on the floor agrees the corridor was empty.
The system lets them in, and then forgets both of them.
The door reads a thumbprint that went home at six.
social: They are walked in, introduced, and offered a drink.
The story is better than the truth and holds up longer.
By the end of it he is asking when they will visit again.
The crew leaves with a name badge and an invitation.

generic: Clean work. The kind nobody will ever hear about.
It goes the way it was drawn on the board.
Professional, unremarkable, and finished on time.
No noise, no marks, no reason to look twice.
The plan holds, which is the whole point of a plan.
stealth: Three rooms, no shadow out of place.
The patrol passes four metres away and keeps walking.
They move in the noise of the building and are part of it.
The floor takes the weight without comment.
athletics: Up, over, and down with breath to spare.
The rig holds and the descent is controlled all the way.
The roller door is cleared before the shift bell.
Hard work, done properly, and quietly.
combat: Short, decisive, and over before anyone reaches a radio.
One down, out of sight, and breathing.
The confrontation resolves without a shot or a shout.
They put him somewhere comfortable and take the keys.
lockpicking: Sixty seconds, and the tumbler gives up its argument.
The cabinet opens without a scratch on the escutcheon.
Steady tension, patient rake, open door.
The safe yields on the second attempt and stays quiet.
hacking: The feed loops for ninety seconds, which is eighty more than needed.
The controller accepts the credentials without asking twice.
In, copied, and out, with the session closed behind them.
The lockout timer resets and nobody is paged.
social: The badge is glanced at, not read.
They are believed, which is all that was required.
A polite conversation, and a door held open at the end of it.
The right name, dropped at the right moment.

generic: They get through. It is not pretty and it is not clean.
The door opens. Something about it will be noticed tomorrow.
Through, but slower than planned and with less margin.
It works, and everyone knows how close it was.
A win by the width of a wrench.
stealth: A footfall lands wrong, and the corridor stays empty anyway.
They freeze for eleven seconds that cost more than the job pays.
Something is knocked, caught, and set down carefully.
The guard turns at the wrong moment and sees an empty hall.
athletics: The grip slips, and holds on the second try.
A hard landing, absorbed badly, and walked off.
They make it up, but the parapet loses some render.
The gap gets crossed with nothing to spare.
combat: It becomes a fight, briefly, and ends in a draw nobody wanted.
He goes down, but not before the radio hits the floor.
They get past. Somebody will have a story and a bruise.
Messy, loud, and survivable.
lockpicking: The lock opens on the fourth attempt, and a pick stays inside it.
It gives, eventually, and leaves a scratch that will be seen.
Two minutes over, and the sweat is a problem for the grip.
Open, but the housing is bent and will not close again.
hacking: In, but the session is logged and the log is not clean.
The loop holds for forty seconds, which is barely enough.
Access granted, alert raised, alert dismissed, for now.
The system lets them through and files a question about it.
social: He believes about half of it, and lets them past anyway.
The story wobbles and is propped up in time.
She waves them through with a look that will be remembered.
Nobody is convinced; nobody quite objects either.

generic: It does not work, and now the room knows somebody tried.
A setback. Recoverable, expensive, and embarrassing.
The plan meets the building and the building wins this one.
They fall back and rethink with less time than before.
No injury, no arrest, no progress.
stealth: A door closes louder than it should and the corridor answers.
They are seen — not identified, but seen.
The floor gives them away and there is nowhere to be.
The patrol turns early and there is no shadow deep enough.
athletics: The grip fails and the drop is short but badly taken.
The rig slips a metre and everything above it hears about it.
Halfway up, out of strength, and back down again.
A bad landing, a turned ankle, and a slow walk to the next door.
combat: It goes to ground, badly, and the radio gets used.
Two of them and both still standing when it matters.
He takes the hit and shouts anyway.
The fight is lost quietly, which is the only mercy in it.
lockpicking: The pick snaps in the keyway and the lock is now a wall.
The tumbler will not set, and the clock does not care.
The plate registers the lift and starts a very short countdown.
Five minutes of nothing, and the shift change coming.
hacking: The credentials are rejected and the rejection is interesting to somebody.
The session drops and the reconnect is flagged.
The camera comes back up early, pointed the wrong way for them.
Access denied, ticket filed, name attached.
social: He does not buy it, and he is polite about calling the desk.
The name is wrong, and she knows exactly how wrong.
A perfectly good story told to a person who checks things.
The conversation ends with a phone being picked up.

generic: Everything that could go wrong does, in order, quickly.
It falls apart in the worst way and takes the schedule with it.
This is the one they will not talk about afterwards.
The job stops being a job and becomes an escape.
Catastrophe, and it is nobody's fault but the dice.
stealth: They walk into a guard, at a distance where explaining is not an option.
The alarm goes, and the building's lights come on floor by floor.
A cleaner opens the door they are standing behind.
Every camera in the wing gets a clear, well-lit face.
athletics: The line parts at eleven metres.
The parapet gives, and so does a wrist.
The fall is long enough to be heard on the street.
They land badly, and the ankle will not take weight.
combat: It becomes exactly the kind of incident this crew does not do.
Somebody is badly hurt, and it is not the guard.
A weapon is drawn, and after that nothing is quiet.
Backup is called on an open channel with a description attached.
lockpicking: The drill slips, the housing screams, and the floor wakes up.
The case seals and locks with the piece still inside it.
The plate goes off, and it is the loud kind.
Broken pick, broken lock, and a door that is now evidence.
hacking: The intrusion is caught live and the floor goes to lockdown.
The shutters come down with the crew on the wrong side of them.
Every door in the building relocks at once.
The system logs the attempt, the source, and the time, in that order.
social: He recognises the face, and he has seen it on a notice.
The lie collapses in front of three people who all repeat it.
She smiles, agrees, and has already pressed the button.
A witness panics, runs, and is believed.
